component.name: Runefin
component.summary: A Jellyfin client drawn entirely by Rune

description.p: Runefin browses a Jellyfin server and plays video in the same window, with no web view and no second render stack.
It has a desktop layout and a Big Screen layout for a TV: a 1280x720 design height, full-screen launch, a 64 pt safe gutter and native gamepad navigation.
The in-app player supports direct play and transcoding, text and bitmap subtitles, chapters, a queue and playback reporting.

screenshot.caption: A library at 1080p with the TV toolbar

description.p: The D-pad reachability test now covers every overlay: the card menu, pre-play sheet, playlist/collection/cast pickers, new-playlist prompt, the still-watching and resume-conflict cards, the shortcut sheet, online subtitle search and the shelf. Each one is a focus surface, so arrows reach every row and Back returns to the opener.

Controller reachability is now a test: every screen and player layer is walked with the D-pad and every visible control must be reachable from the first focus. The test found and fixed real dead ends — Settings opened on a key that was never drawn, the library toolbar and filter sheet, search's sidebar and See all, Live TV's toolbar and row buttons, the detail version/tech/IMDb controls, and the player's Back, seek buttons and queue.

TV navigation: the player's gear sheet and every panel take focus, Back returns to the row that opened them instead of the page behind, Settings section chips move the selector into their section, and a movie detail reaches its cast, extras and similar titles below the actions. Vertical moves glide the page. The focused timeline and volume use a larger ringed knob rather than a wash, and big screen launches at 16:9.

Cards carry an EXTRA badge when the item has special features, read from the server's SpecialFeatureCount field. And optional silent hover previews: after a second on a poster, the card cycles the item's own trickplay frames through the middle of its runtime with a PREVIEW timestamp. Off by default, no audio and no second player, and it keeps only one tile in memory.

The library filter sheet adds studio, tag and, for series, Continuing/Ended. Filters are now removable chips above the grid with Clear all, and the Filters button counts the active ones. Studio and tag lists come from the server once per library.

In name order the library pins the first visible row's letter at the top-left, so a long grid or list always says where the reader is. It sits with the back-to-top pill and the Attention panel from 0.1.26.

The library heading now summarises the view from exact server counts: items, unwatched, missing and total runtime. An Attention chip appears when items are missing or unaired, with a one-click filter for each, and a back-to-top pill returns to the first row after a long scroll.

The optional compact Home hero is now part of the focus order: it takes the first focus when enabled, Up from any rail reaches it, and it uses its own entry's backdrop. Its subtitle names the episode and the time left, and a hidden entry is skipped.

End of episode: the episode shrinks to a corner over a dimmed next still while a card offers Play now, Watch credits and Dismiss, with the next episode's runtime, overview and countdown. The card takes focus from the timeline.
PlaybackInfo's Why line now names the real reason: the chosen bitrate cap versus the file, or the codec and container the device profile refused.
The focus halo is painted at the window root instead of inside the rail, so it is complete above, below and to the left of the poster; it is smaller and leaves the artwork unwashed.
The card halo is smaller and has room above and below the poster, so focus glows on all four sides rather than only left and right.

A UI polish pass: settings groups, Live TV channels, Remote sessions, Seerr request rows and the Detail Next up card get a top sheen and an inset edge; actions gain their sheen and shadow; cards spring their hover outline; menus and the toast rise as they enter.

Card focus is the pointer's hover treatment on every rail: a rounded white outline, the play/remove affordance and a soft halo, with no scale and no fill. The volume slider keeps Up/Down for the level so Left/Right reach the gear.

A focused card now lifts 6% instead of showing a box, the player's volume slider moves on with Left/Right so the gear is reachable, and the Detail page's action, Next up and season controls are all focus targets.
The Person error state's retry button keeps the same hover-wash focus as every other control.

Big-screen focus now reads like pointer hover: the neutral wash alone, with no ring around cards, sidebar rows or buttons, and every Detail action, the Next up card and the season controls are reachable.

The focus router now runs before Rune's own arrow handling, so the TV zones actually receive the keys. The player's timeline scrubs with Left/Right and commits with OK, the OSD opens on the timeline, and two big-screen focus snapshots pin the visuals.

Seerr's detail page joins the focus router: Back, the action row, the season picker and the cast rail, matching what the page actually draws. The router now also claims every screen it owns at the edges, and entering a rail from a vertical list starts at its first item.
Live TV and Remote join the focus router, and panels, menus and scrollbars keep their own directions instead of being swallowed by it.
Focus zones for Search, Person and Seerr, and directional navigation in Settings follows the page's tab order. The living-room router now covers every main screen except Live TV and Remote.

The living-room focus model: lanes switch with Up/Down, Left returns to the sidebar, edges clamp, the detail page and the player OSD take the D-pad, a CEC remote's OK plays and pauses, and focus is a neutral wash instead of a blue box.

Statistics shows the negotiated colour facts (transfer, matrix, mastering luminance, content light level), and a Dolby Vision title now says when the server is tone-mapping it instead of leaving the transcode unexplained.

Subtitle timing follows a transcoded stream that starts at the resume point, and seeks stay in file time. Dolby Vision files are tone-mapped by the server, and a direct play with no frame retries transcoded.
A failed playback names the method (DirectPlay, DirectStream or Transcode) and says when the stream ended before its first frame, and the error wraps instead of running off the screen.

The integrated player keeps waiting while a stream is still starting instead of falling back to mpv after a couple of seconds, and a failed fallback now names both the GStreamer reason and the mpv one.

Fixes big-screen input: the focus request made when a screen opens was dropped, so arrows, the D-pad and OK did nothing and only Back worked. A focused card now shows its ring again and activates with OK.

Updated to the latest Rune revision: text wraps as Chromium wraps it, text fields take IME composition, tooltips follow a new timing model, and long libraries scroll without rows jumping as content passes.

A TV remote's OK button (Return) now presses the focused control everywhere on the big screen, and the CEC helper only maps the Menu buttons so it no longer changes what OK and the D-pad do in the Steam UI.
Playback keeps its pacing: a late frame is dropped instead of replayed, and the player clock is read ten times a second rather than every frame.
